propositions: CLI --output json emits nanosecond timestamps (created_at, updated_at, comment timestamps) as bare JSON integers exceeding RFC 8259 §6 safe range (|n| > 2^53-1), causing silent rounding in float64 consumers (jq, Node, Ruby) and serialization failure in BigInt consumers.

The MCP surface was fixed via js_safe_result conversion (ticket 6fe7) but CLI was deliberately left out of scope, creating a parity gap where the same wire-shape hazard exists on the publicly-documented "strongest contract" surface where users pipe rebar JSON into jq.

Remediation applies js_safe_dumps (json.dumps(js_safe_result(value))) as a single choke point across all 50+ CLI --output json/llm emitters, converting out-of-range integers to exact decimal strings while preserving in-range values unchanged, making the conversion lossless.

An AST guard (scripts/check_cli_json_js_safe.py) wired into make lint fails if any future CLI stdout emitter calls raw json.dumps on store data without js-safe conversion, preventing silent reintroduction of the hazard.

The schema already types created_at/updated_at as ["integer","string","null"] and prescribes the string wire form for out-of-range values; CLI conversion makes this prose literally true across all three surfaces (MCP, CLI, schema).
